planner.bar_note: The optimiser makes a move only when it gains more than 1.0 expected points over the rest of the plan (5 if it costs a -4 hit), so it doesn't churn on small differences.

wildcard.why: After the round of 16, half the clubs are out. MD11 already has unlimited transfers, so the Wildcard is most useful at a quarter-final or semi-final first leg (MD13 or MD15), if more of your players are out than your 5 free transfers can replace.

limitless.why: Only two clubs play the final and the club limit rises to 8, so a one-day team with no budget limit can be filled with the best players of both finalists.

chips.summary: Keep both chips for the knockouts: the best use before the play-offs (wildcard on MD7) is worth only 3.4 points, against what they can do at the quarter-finals and the final.

between_days.note: Between-days advice appears after the first match day.

how_it_works: Team strength: every club's attack and defence are rated from its Champions League matches (2025/26 at half weight).

A second rating uses every match: domestic league results from 13 leagues and the European ones, updated match by match like Elo, with each league's strength learned from European matches between leagues. Clubs from Czechia, Slovakia, Ukraine, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan and Cyprus only have their European matches (no free source for their leagues).
That all-matches rating sets what a player with few Champions League minutes is expected to do and 50% of the knockout chances.

Players: chance of starting and of playing 60+ minutes from his club's recent matches and UEFA's injury news; goals, assists, balls recovered, saves and the rest per 90 minutes from his Champions League matches, pulled towards a typical player in his position as if he had 3 extra average matches. That pull fades as his own minutes grow.

Each expected count becomes points with UEFA's exact scoring rules; goals and assists rise with how many goals his club should score in that match, clean sheets with how few it should concede. Bookmaker odds are blended in when available close to the matchday.
Every change to the model is backtested on 2025/26 and on this season's matchdays it hadn't seen, and kept only if it helps on both.

plain: Replayed 19 matchdays, predicting each one only from the matches before it.
Ranking the players who started: 0.18 for XPert against 0.11 for points per game so far (1 = perfect order, 0 = random).
Of the 10 players we expected to score most, 1.7 on average were in the real top 10 (points per game: 1.6). They scored 5.2 points each on average (4.5).
Our captain pick scored 7.3 points on average (points per game's pick: 3.7), before doubling.
backtest.method: Each matchday predicted only from matches before it; injury news not used (not stored historically).
